snp3.8:4.4: See the verse at the end of DN 16, part III.
snp3.8:17.4: These lines can also be read as an imperative: “So, having heard the arahant, subdue lamentation; seeing the dead one whose time is done, [and thinking,] ‘I can’t fetch him back.’”
snp3.8:19.4: These lines can also be construed with the previous verse, so that it is the enlightened one’s own lamentation, longing, & sorrow that get blown away like cotton fluff, leaving this verse to read simply: “Seeking your own happiness, you should pull out your own arrow.”
